test.name: person_quality answers a non-FamilySearch id itself; the report leaves quality out
test.description: User asks to check Patrick Flynn, whose tree id is 'I1' — a project id, not a FamilySearch person id. The skill runs person_warnings and person_quality for him as for anyone; person_quality answers reason 'not_familysearch_id' without contacting FamilySearch. The tool looks Patrick up in the project tree, finds no FamilySearch link, and answers with one sentence by name; the report writes that sentence exactly, never naming the id or its type.

input.user_message: Check Patrick Flynn for any warnings.

judge_context: Should call person_quality with personId 'I1' and projectPath. The tool answers {ok: false, reason: 'not_familysearch_id', errors: ['Patrick Flynn isn't linked to FamilySearch, so there's no FamilySearch quality score.']} without contacting FamilySearch; that answer is not a failure.
Should report the person_warnings result (no impossibilities)

Should write the tool's sentence as the FamilySearch quality line. A heading above it or true advice after it (e.g. that linking the person to FamilySearch would give a score) is fine. What must not appear is any description of the id or its type — the deterministic validator test_not_fs_reply_names_no_id grades that, not the judge.
